headlines.title: Supply chain inflation: How rising diesel prices will impact consumers
headlines.description: Get ready for the domino effect from rising fuel prices. Diesel prices are now hovering at record levels and experts warn of “supply chain inflation” where the increased costs will be passed on to customers. NBC Bay Area’s Damian Trujillo has more in the video above. headlines.title: Vallejo conservationist says she was unjustly arrested while volunteering
headlines.description: A well-known North Bay conservationist says she was unjustly arrested and manhandled on Wednesday while doing the volunteer duties she’s been doing for years. Myrna Hayes, 70, of Vallejo, was arrested at Mare Island’s San Pablo Bay Trail on Wednesday during her nightly routine of locking the gates to the trail. “I’ve been locking this gate. I go 3/4 of a mile on the gravel road every night, going on 17 years,” Hayes said. Vallejo police say they were responding to a report of suspicious activity that night, and the 70-year-old was arrested after she ran up on them. Hayes says she initially didn’t realize they were police and was trying to clear the park before locking it. “That’s when he physically grabbed me and handcuffed me,” she said. “I know that he took me another time and smashed me against his car.” Hayes says the encounter left her with a bruised eye, swollen legs and body pains. Three patrols cars and six officers responded to the scene. Hayes was taken to jail, where she spent 12 hours before being released Thursday morning. Hayes says she’s baffled and angry. “I’ve never been in jail. I’ve never been touched by a police officer. I’ve never been charged with anything other than a speeding ticket in college,” she said. Civil Rights Attorney Melissa Nold believes the police response is bizarre, adding a 70-year-old unarmed woman didn’t warrant this kind of escalation. “Everyone knows Myrna everybody loves Myrna. She’s a kind soul,” Nold said. “You’re supposed to take the path of least resistance, not go turbo charge when you’re dealing with a 70-year-old woman who’s been out here serving our community for decades.” Hayes has been serving as the unpaid caretaker and tour guide for Mare Island shoreline for three decades and was even featured on NBC Bay Area’s “Bay Area Proud” for being a steward of the wetlands. She says the encounter with the police has left her shaken. NBC Bay Area reached out to Vallejo police and the city for comment but did not hear back. Hayes is scheduled to be arraigned on obstruction charges in November.

headlines.title: Bicyclist fatally struck in San Jose
headlines.description: A female bicyclist was killed after being struck by a vehicle in San Jose early Friday morning, according to police. The collision happened around 6:15 a.m. in the area of East Capitol Expressway and Ocala Avenue. Police said a 2017 white Ford F-350 pickup truck, operated by an adult male driver, was traveling northbound on Capitol Expressway through its intersection with Ocala Avenue on a greenlight when it struck an adult female bicyclist traveling eastbound on Ocala Avenue. The bicyclist died from their injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene, police said. Police initially were called to respond to a hit-and-run collision but eventually made contact with the driver, who waited to exit safely from the expressway. Drugs or alcohol are not considered to be a factor, police said. The incident marks the city’s 37th fatal collision and 37th traffic-related death of 2026. Anyone with information is urged to contact Detective DelliCarpini #4103 of the San José Police Department’s Traffic Investigations Unit at 4103@sanjoseca.gov or 408-277-4654.

headlines.title: San Jose Starbucks among 250 stores closing across North America
headlines.description: A Starbucks in San Jose is one of the 250 stores expected to close in North America. The Starbucks at 1205 The Alameda in San Jose is expected to close on Saturday. Jennifer Martinez and Rebecca Schroeder took their coffee break and made their usual trip to the shop, knowing it would be the last time. “It was very abrupt. We didn’t even know until a coworker came and told us just right now, so we came over to say goodbye to the folks who work here, because they’ve been so great every morning,” Schroeder said. “I understand, I think, from a business perspective that they probably did it because they didn’t want everyone quitting or bailing, but the ‘human’ side of it is really… it’s harsh,” Martinez said. San Jose State University economist Robert Chapman Wood says that bond with customers was somewhat lost when Starbucks founder Howard Schultz retired. It is a bit of business magic that’s hard to duplicate. “The whole thing about creating a relationship between thousands of people in hundreds of thousands of people in tens of thousands of stores and the customers who walk in, that’s not something that any professor can tell you how to do,” Wood said. Starbucks says it plans to revamp many stores to offer a more inviting, traditional coffeehouse feel. “It definitely depends for Starbucks on creating that atmosphere people will choose to go to, as opposed to just producing coffee, because other places produce coffee for less money than Starbucks,” Wood said. But for those used to this neighborhood Starbucks, what can’t be recreated is convenience, even though the next closest Starbucks is only 0.7 miles away. There are still about 18,000 Starbucks stores in North America. The Bay Area Starbucks expected to close, according to the Business Times, include: 3547 Mt. Diablo Blvd. in Lafayette 1663 N. California Blvd. in Walnut Creek 176 Gateway Blvd. in South San Francisco 138 Calistoga Rd. in Santa Rosa 2240 Mendocino Ave. in Santa Rosa 1187 San Carlos Ave. in San Carlos 119 N. headlines.title: 49ers star edge rusher Nick Bosa out ‘few weeks' after pulling calf, per report
headlines.description: The 49ers again will be without star edge rusher Nick Bosa for an extended period. Bosa pulled his calf during practice this week and will miss “a few weeks,” ESPN’s Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported Friday, citing sources. Bosa played on 63 percent of the 49ers’ defensive snaps during the first two games of the season, but he popped up on the injury report Thursday. NBC Sports Bay Area’s Jennifer Lee Chan hinted at a potentially serious Bosa injury late Thursday. “Nick Bosa was supposed to talk to us on Wednesday,” Chan said during a YouTube live stream. “That was his media day. He did not talk to us on Wednesday and then he did not talk to us today, Thursday. We waited around for him. And … knee and calf. It’s not good. I just don’t think … It doesn’t feel good. Like, my spidey senses are saying that this is a serious injury for Nick Bosa, and if he’s not out for the season, he’s out for multiple weeks.” At least for the moment, it appears Bosa and the 49ers dodged the “out for the season” bullet. Bosa missed most of the 2025 NFL season after tearing his ACL early in the year. Bosa’s injury is the latest blow to the 49ers’ defensive line, with Alfred Collins already out for the season, and Sam Okuayinonu and CJ West on injured reserve. James Thompson Jr. is expected to miss time with an ankle injury and rookie Romello Height underwent surgery for a fractured hand, putting his status for Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals in doubt. The 49ers had big expectations for Bosa this season and now he will be sidelined for several weeks. headlines.title: New biotech startup at Stanford is run by thousands of AI agents
headlines.description: A brand-new biotech startup with thousands of AI agents is sprouting at Stanford. Stanford professor and AI researcher Dr. James Zou runs the virtual biotech lab. The startup was launched by humans, but it is run by AI agents. The work at the biotech startup is done at a physical lab, but the research is done by AI agents that have been trained and programmed to do it. “AI is coming up with hypotheses, questions, telling us how to design experiments, actually acting more like a partner, a colleague,” Zou said. According to the professor, the startup has more than 30,000 AI agents. The goal of the startup is not to replace humans in the lab but to give humans more time to work on what they do best. “You want the human scientists to really focus on the more creative aspects of discovery,” Zou said. Humans are also needed to keep track of the AI agents, watching their every move so none of them go rogue. The AI agents can take on different personalities while working in the virtual lab. Some of the agents become leaders, others become critics. The human scientists said it’s actually a very similar dynamic to what they see in a physical lab.

headlines.title: 3 hospitalized, dozens displaced after apartment fire in Oakland
headlines.description: Dozens of people were displaced and three were hospitalized after an early morning fire at an apartment complex in Oakland on Friday. The three-alarm fire broke out on Bancroft Avenue near 51st Avenue and International Boulevard just before 1 a.m. Fire crews rescued several people from the second floor of the building. Three people were taken to a nearby hospital. The fire has since been extinguished. The cause of the fire was not immediately known.

headlines.title: Tom Holland, Oakland native Zendaya spotted in Marin County
headlines.description: Fresh off a busy summer, actors Tom Holland and Oakland native Zendaya have been spotted spending time in the North Bay. Video posted on TikTok showed the pair walking at The Village at Corte Madera earlier this week. On Thursday, Holland also snapped a selfie with servers at Mixt, a salad chain in Mill Valley. The newlyweds co-starred in two major blockbusters this summer, “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” Their appearances come as social media has been filled with rumors that the couple bought a home in Tiburon.

headlines.title: Hundreds celebrate Dolly Parton Day in San Francisco's Union Square
headlines.description: Hundreds of people gathered at San Francisco’s Union Square on Friday to celebrate Dolly Parton Day. Sept. 25, or 9/25, was dubbed Dolly Parton Day in cities across America. In San Francisco, the celebration featured blonde wigs, pink sparkles and fans channeling their inner Dolly. “It’s really especially good when you’re a middle-aged woman and you kinda get to that point where you feel a little bit invisible,” Santa Cruz resident Robin Searles said. “Then you throw this bad boy on and you are no longer invisible.” Several people also competed in the first-ever Dolly Parton Day look-alike contest. Even a parakeet joined in, wearing a hot pink hat. Oakland resident Linda Dardarian said she doesn’t know anyone who doesn’t like Parton. “In such divisive times, it’s almost miraculous that one person can have so much crossover appeal,” Dardarian said. “And I think it’s because of her love and positivity.” The celebration also included firsthand stories from a man who drove Parton’s limousine around San Francisco, a “Tonight Show” musician who met her several times and an anthropologist who teaches a college course on Dolly-ology. “I think it’s really inspiring for students right now in this day and age when they’re being pulled in so many directions, when social media wants them to be A, B and C, they look at Dolly and say, I can be who I want to be,” Indiana University anthropologist Sarah Phillips said. The San Francisco Public Library also participated as a partner of Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library. People can donate to help fund the program, and parents can sign up their children to receive free books through the project.

headlines.title: Family, friends continue search 6 months after Amy Hillyard disappeared
headlines.description: The husband of missing coffee shop owner Amy Hillyard issued an appeal to keep her story visible, on the six-month anniversary of her disappearance in March. Chris Hillyard said in a video that investigators and supporters continue to search for answers, and are focusing the search on specific areas, using drones to hunt for clues in areas where Amy liked to hike and walk. “The private investigator who’s worked on missing persons cases across the country called Amy’s disappearance one of the most perplexing cases he’s ever worked on,” Chris Hillyard said in the video. The owner of Farley’s coffee shops in Oakland and San Francisco, 52-year-old Amy Hillyard was last seen on March 25, sometime after 2 p.m. near the 500 block of Radnor Road in Oakland. Amy is described as white, 5 feet 4 inches tall, weighing about 120 pounds, with blonde hair and hazel eyes. She was wearing a white short-sleeved shirt, light-colored jeans, and white sneakers with black stripes. She is considered at risk due to a medical condition. It’s been six months and her friends and family haven’t given up on the search. “Still we all keep trying and every day we wake up with a glimmer of hope that today will the day that brings some piece of information that offers an answer to Amy’s whereabouts,” Chris Hillyard said. A $25,000 reward for information on Hillyard’s disappearance is still in effect. The video can be found at https://www.youtube.com/shorts/ajqClXNBv48 and at Bringamyhome.com, a site created by Amy’s friends and family where supporters can stay up to date on the status of current efforts to find Hillyard. The site also has various ways that people can help in the search.

headlines.title: San Francisco Fleet Week 2026: Events, schedules, what to know
headlines.description: It’s that time of year again. San Francisco Fleet Week is back. The fall tradition will be highlighted by the Blue Angels screaming across the skies, but there are plenty of other events to experience. Check out the guide below to learn more about Fleet Week events. What is San Francisco Fleet Week? San Francisco Fleet Week is an annual celebration of the nation’s sea services. A multi-day air show, parade of ships and ship tours highlight the weeklong festivities. “San Francisco Fleet Week is an annual public event that honors the contributions of the men and women of the United States Armed Forces while advancing cooperation and knowledge among civilian- and military-based Humanitarian Assistance personnel,” a statement on the event’s website reads. When is San Francisco Fleet Week 2026? Fleet Week is scheduled to take place Sunday, Oct. 4 through Monday, Oct. 12. headlines.title: Bay Area gas prices jump about 70 cents in a month
headlines.description: Drivers across the Bay Area are paying significantly more at the pump than they were a month ago, according to new numbers from AAA. The average price for a gallon of gas in California jumped another 15 cents over the past week to $6.23. Prices are even higher in parts of the Bay Area. In Oakland, the average price is $6.35 a gallon, up from $5.61 a month ago. San Francisco’s average climbed to $6.47 from $5.74, while San Jose’s rose to $6.30 from $5.57. That’s an increase of around 70 cents a gallon in just one month. Some individual stations are charging even more. A Chevron station in Dublin was charging $6.79 a gallon Friday morning, while a Shell station in San Francisco was charging $7.29. Nationwide, the average price for a gallon of gas is $4.48, the highest the national average has ever been for this time of year. NBC Bay Area’s Bob Redell has the full report in the video above.
